title: A Drop for the Contact
premise: Casper Reyes, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering his own conscience by burying cases against the powerful, discovers the government safe house protecting him has been listed for sale online — interior photos and all — a message that someone inside the system sold him out. Hunted by both the cartel fixer he once investigated and the federal handler who betrayed him, Casper goes dark with a burned-out journalist and a teenage hacker who become the family he never had. To survive, he must trade the ledger of bribes he copied years ago — the one secret worth killing for — at the global anti-corruption summit where his betrayer will be standing beside the people it implicates. In the end, Casper releases the ledger publicly rather than trade it for his own safety, burning his old life to ash but walking away alive, unimportant, and finally clean.
about_author: Dominic Okafor is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems built to protect the guilty.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper closes another whitewashed case against a senator's donor, then drives to a storage unit where his go-bag waits — cash, burner phones, a false passport under the name Daniel Voss. The emotional beat is quiet dread: he has everything a corrupt man would want and nothing a good man could keep.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A real-estate alert pings his burner: the safe house where he testified three years ago is listed for sale — with photos of the interior, including the closet where his old case files were stored. He recognizes the staging: someone wanted him to see it. Beat: cold recognition that his protection is now bait.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper confronts his federal handler, Marisol Vance, who insists the listing is a clerical error and orders him to stay visible until the summit security sweep ends. Her calm is too rehearsed. Beat: suspicion curdling into certainty as he notices her new watch costs more than his annual salary.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: POV: Teodor Brankov. The cartel's financial fixer reviews the safe-house photos and confirms the man in the reflection of a window frame is Casper Reyes. He gives his team forty-eight hours and one instruction: no body, just the ledger. Beat: patient menace; the hunter who never hurries.

chapters.title: Go-Bag
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper runs his own counter-surveillance and finds a GPS tracker sewn into his car's headliner — placed during its last 'service' authorized by Vance. He leaves the tracker in a laundromat and takes the bag. Beat: grief disguised as efficiency as he abandons his apartment and identity.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia Okonkwo. A disgraced investigative journalist working a food-truck shift spots Casper buying a prepaid phone and follows him on instinct — she spent two years chasing the same ledger rumor before her editor killed the story. She offers what she knows in exchange for the story. Beat: wary alliance between two people who trust nothing.

chapters.title: Pixel
chapters.summary: POV: Pixel (Jules). Seventeen-year-old hacker Jules, who found the real-estate listing anomaly in the first place, decrypts the MLS metadata: the photos were uploaded from an account belonging to the U.S. Marshals Service. Beat: exhilaration tipping into fear when they realize they've touched something federal.

chapters.title: Three Strangers
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The trio holes up in a shuttered motel; Casper lays out the truth — the ledger he copied names officials across three continents, and the summit in ten days will ratify an anti-corruption framework those same officials wrote. Beat: fragile found-family forming over takeout containers and shared paranoia.

chapters.title: The Laundromat Trap
chapters.summary: POV: Teodor. Brankov's team sweeps the abandoned tracker site, finds the laundromat cameras, and pulls a partial face of Nadia. Instead of raiding, Brankov lets them run — a watched fugitive leads to the ledger faster than a dead one. Beat: the trap tightening without the prey feeling it.

chapters.title: What Vance Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol Vance. Vance reports to a voice above her that Reyes is mobile but contained; we learn she sold the safe house listing herself, on orders, believing Casper's ledger would be quietly recovered and buried. Beat: complicity rationalized — she tells herself she's saving the system, not selling a man.

chapters.title: Shell Game
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Following money instead of hiding from it, Casper traces the brokerage that listed the safe house through four shells to a Cayman entity whose beneficial owner matches a name in his own ledger. Beat: grim vindication — the conspiracy used his own map against him.

chapters.title: Safe House
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. The team breaks into the actual listed safe house to retrieve the physical backup Casper hid there years ago — and walks into Brankov's surveillance perimeter. They escape through the crawl space with the drive, but Pixel is filmed. Beat: victory that feels like exposure.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: POV: Pixel. Brankov's people find Jules's foster home and make a quiet offer: the ledger for the kid's record wiped clean. Jules refuses but doesn't tell the others, carrying the threat alone. Beat: the loneliness of being the youngest and most expendable.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Vance contacts Casper through a dead-drop protocol only they knew: turn over the ledger before the summit and receive immunity and a new life. Casper realizes the offer proves the summit's architects are the ledger's subjects. Beat: temptation met with clarity.

chapters.title: Interlude: Daniel Voss
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In a long night vigil, Casper reads his own forged passport and remembers the honest investigator he was before the first buried case. Nadia finds him awake and they trade histories honestly for the first time. Beat: intimacy as anchor; choosing who he'll be before choosing what he'll do.

chapters.title: Summit City
chapters.summary: POV: multiple, braided. The team infiltrates the summit host city amid delegations and closed streets; Brankov arrives with diplomatic cover; Vance prepares the handoff team. Beat: converging vectors — every player now within a square mile of each other.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper agrees to meet Vance's exchange point, intending to feed her a decoy drive while Nadia and Pixel upload the real ledger to a distributed archive timed to release during the summit's closing session. Beat: high-wire tension as the deception unfolds in real time.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Twice
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. Brankov's team hits the exchange simultaneously with Vance's — Vance realizes she was always disposable — and in the chaos Pixel is taken while uploading. Nadia gets the final packet out but loses Jules. Beat: triumph and catastrophe in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Live
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. During the summit's closing plenary, the ledger floods delegates' screens and every newsroom on earth: names, accounts, signatures. Brankov's employers burn their own fixer; Brankov, exposed, chooses survival over the contract and lets Pixel go. Beat: catharsis — power devouring its own servants.

chapters.title: Vance's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol Vance. Cornered by both her superiors and federal investigators, Vance hands Casper the evidence that convicts the chain above her, accepting arrest. Her last words to him: 'You were the case I should have kept.' Beat: tragic accountability; corruption's cost paid personally.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. Arrests cascade across three continents; Nadia's story resurrects her career, but she declines the byline glory to shield Pixel and Casper from grand-jury exposure. Beat: justice outside the law proving messier and truer than the official kind.

chapters.title: A Drop for the Contact
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Months later, Casper — legally dead, living under no name at all — makes one last dead drop: not documents, but a postcard to Nadia and Jules, the closest thing to family he has. He keeps a go-bag packed out of habit, then unpacks it. Beat: quiet resolution; a man finally still enough to stay.
